records.title: Neural architecture search for adversarial robustness via learnable pruning
records.reason: ANAS-P learns per-layer convolution width masks during adversarial training/pruning and fine-tunes sparse ResNet/VGG models. Evaluation uses CIFAR-10/100 and TinyImageNet with TRADES/MART across sparsity levels, measuring clean and robust accuracy. It is CNN robustness, not transformer/LLM inference; shared pruning/FPGA lineage is too broad.

records.title: Estimating the Energy Footprint of Software Systems: a Primer
records.reason: This primer describes approaches and methodological pitfalls for estimating software energy, comparing measurement/estimation methods and reporting practical experiment considerations. It offers no new LLM inference optimization or LLM-specific empirical result. It could inform evaluation of the linked green-inference work, but is a generic measurement guide rather than a technical lineage contribution.

records.title: Read Ten Lines at One Glance: Line-Aware Semi-Autoregressive Transformer for Multi-Line Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
records.reason: Tried the ACM DOI/publisher record; the full paper body was not accessible, so method details, evaluation tables and limitations could not be verified. The abstract describes a line-aware semi-autoregressive decoder for handwritten multi-line math with claimed faster decoding and state-of-the-art recognition. Because primary full text was unavailable, retain as reasoned borderline pending an author or institutional copy.

records.title: Perceptional and actional enrichment for metaphor detection with sensorimotor norms
records.reason: The authors enrich word representations with sensorimotor norms and test metaphor detection on VUA and TOEFL corpora, comparing feature/model families and interpretability. The goal and evaluations concern figurative-language classification, not model compression or inference efficiency; the linked Q8BERT line has no method-level connection.

records.title: Mobile Accelerator Exploiting Sparsity of Multi-Heads, Lines, and Blocks in Transformers in Computer Vision
records.reason: The author-hosted DATE proceedings PDF timed out on retrieval. The paper abstract describes a mobile accelerator for vision transformers with head-wise, line-wise and block-wise sparsity, a head scheduler and sparse GEMM, reporting energy-efficiency improvements on DETR/ViT. Primary method/evaluation/limitations could not be reviewed; leave borderline until full text is available.
